mercy_translation.text:
God not only made us from nothing; through the grace of the Word he also granted us to live according to God. But human beings turned away from eternal things and, by the counsel of the devil, turned toward things subject to corruption. Thus they became the cause of their own corruption in death. As I said before, they were by nature corruptible, but by the grace of participation in the Word they had escaped what belonged to their nature, if only they had remained good.

For because the Word was present with them, their natural corruption did not come near them, as Wisdom also says: “God created the human being for incorruption and made him an image of his own eternity; but through the envy of the devil death entered the world.” Once this happened, human beings died, and corruption thereafter flourished against them, becoming stronger than what belonged to nature throughout the whole race, because it had also obtained against them the force of the divine threat on account of their transgression of the commandment.

For in their offenses human beings did not stop within fixed limits. By progressing little by little they finally went beyond all measure. From the beginning they became inventors of wickedness and brought death and corruption upon themselves; later, turning aside into injustice and surpassing every lawlessness, never stopping at one evil but continually inventing new evils upon old, they became insatiable in sinning.

Adulteries and thefts were everywhere; the whole earth was full of murders and robberies. No concern was given to law in matters of corruption and injustice. Every kind of evil was practiced by everyone, individually and collectively. Cities made war against cities, nations rose against nations, and the whole inhabited world was torn by factions and battles, each one contending in lawlessness.

Nor were acts contrary to nature far removed from these things. As the Apostle, Christ’s witness, said: “Their women exchanged natural relations for those contrary to nature; and likewise the men, leaving natural relations with women, were inflamed in their desire for one another, men committing shameless acts with men and receiving in themselves the due recompense of their error.”

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
Biblical citations are translated from Athanasius' Greek wording in this chapter.
The moral catalogue belongs to Athanasius' account of the progressive disorder of humanity after turning from God.
